newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra posts mixed first-half results.
newsitem.headline: Astra posts mixed first-half results.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra AB said Friday its pre-tax profit rose 4 percent to 7.01 billion crowns ($881.6 million) in the first six months, slightly lower than market expectations of 7.18 billion crowns ($904.2 million).
Astra said its sales rose 13 percent to 21.47 billion crowns ($2.7 billion), with North American markets showing the strongest growth while European markets were mixed.
However, calculated at constant exchange rates, sales rose by only 6 percent, Astra said.
North American sales rose to 6.33 billion crowns ($796 million) from 4.81 billion crowns ($605 million), Astra said. Calculated at constant currency rates, the rise was 18 percent.
"A large part of the group's sales growth is now derived from North America, where several of Astra's products are expected to have substantial further potential," Astra said.
The company reported operating profit of 6.75 billion crowns ($849 million) against 6.30 billion crowns ($792 million) in the same period a year ago.
Astra said its sales in Europe rose slightly to 11.66 billion crowns ($1.55 billion) from 11.22 billion crowns ($1.41 billion).
Sales of its biggest product, the anti-peptic ulcer agent Losec, rose to 14.72 billion crowns ($1.85 billion) worldwide from 11.78 billion crowns ($1.48 billion).
Astra's own sales of Losec, which it jointly markets with Merck & Co. Inc. as Prilosec in the United States, rose to 10.12 billion crowns ($1.27 billion) from 8.55 billion crowns ($1.08 billion).
Sales of the antiasthma agenct Pulmicort rose 8 percent to 2.48 billion crowns ($312 million).

Astra said its beta-blocker Seloken, its largest product in the cardiovascular area, rose 19 percent to 1.48 billion crowns ($186 million) and was showing rapid growth mainly due to a favourable trend in the United States.
